attribution.note: Marcus's own words on his Substack, listing things he doubts AI will do by end of 2025. Not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised text states a firm 'will not' and drops 'master'. The source says 'seriously doubt', and the post adds that some items 'might get checked off'. That is a hedged expectation for each item, not a firm commitment. It stays a forecast in kind but is graded confidence, so it is not scored.

contract.note: The contract rests on the speaker's own caveat, 'I could be wrong on a few' and 'some items might get checked off'. It fairly treats this item as unscored. The firm claim (not all items) is separate. The reading is grounded in the speaker's words.

output.rationale: The horizon (end of 2025) has passed, but the item is hedged. 'Seriously doubt', together with the post's explicit allowance that some items might be achieved, makes this a graded per-item expectation rather than a firm forecast. Under policy it is not scored.
